message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the most recent common ancestor of the two major mammalian clades that contain them: **Carnivora** (the order that includes lions) and **Perissodactyla** (the order that includes zebras).  

In other words, the common ancestor is a member of the broader group of placental mammals (Eutheria) that lived roughly 100–120 million years ago, before the lineages that would become modern carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates diverged. This ancestor would have been a small, insect‑eating mammal that lived in the late Cretaceous or early Paleogene.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want the common ancestor of lion and zebra. We need to answer. The user didn't ask for a function call. There's no function relevant. So we just answer. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) is the last common ancestor of the family Felidae and Equidae. They belong to the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla respectively. The last common ancestor would be a mammal from the group of early mammals, maybe the last common ancestor of placental mammals? Actually lion is a carnivore, zebra is a perissodactyl. They diverged earlier. The last common ancestor of all placental mammals is the last common ancestor of the two orders. That would be a mammal from the group of early placentals, maybe the last common ancestor of the clade of placental mammals (Eutheria). But we can say the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is a mammal that lived around 100 million years ago, likely a small, insectivorous mammal. But we can be more precise: The last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the clades Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That ancestor would have lived in the late Cretaceous or early Paleogene. So answer: The last common ancestor of lion and zebra is a mammal from the group of early placental mammals, likely a small insectivore that lived around 100 million years ago. Or we can say the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the clade of placental mammals, which is the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. So answer accordingly.
